title: Annotatio VI §.I: sacramental Oral eating — intrinsic substance vs extrinsic bread-seal
pass_a_gloss: Therefore Eating of Christ’s body, Sacramental, standing for Oral, can be taken in a double sense: either thus, that the denomination from Christ’s body as its Object is intrinsic to it, and the Eating touches the very Substance of Christ’s body; or thus, that the same denomination regards Christ’s body only extrinsically and is called Sacramental Eating of Christ’s body, not because it is Substantial of Christ’s body itself, but rather Eating of this Body’s Sacrament — i.e. of the blessed bread representing Christ’s body.
pass_b_english: Sacramental eating (standing for Oral) has two senses.

Intrinsic: the name reaches Christ’s body as object and touches its substance. Extrinsic: it only regards Christ’s body from outside — eating the sacrament of that body, the blessed bread that represents it.
source_text: Itaque Manducatio corporis Christi, Sacramentalis, pro Orali supponens, duplici sensu accipi potest, vel hôc, ut denominatio à corpore Christi, ceu Objecto ejus, ei intrinseca sit, ipsámque corporis Christi Substantiam Manducatio attingat; vel istô, ut denominatio eadem Christi corpus extrinsece duntaxat respiciat & Sacramentalis corporis Christi Manducatio audiat, non quòd ipsius corporis Christi Substantialis, sed Sacramenti potiùs hujus Corporis, i. e. panis benedicti, Christi corpus repræsentantis, Manducatio existat.
